t: Appropriations made by section 101 shall be available to the extent and in the manner which would be provided by the pertinent appropriations Act.

fable.w: This provision only governs how appropriated funds are made available, by reference to the pertinent appropriations Act. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: Appropriations made by section 101 shall be available to the extent and in the manner which would be provided by the pertinent appropriations Act.

opus.w: This provision only says that appropriations made by section 101 are available as the relevant appropriations Act would provide. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any decision. It does not create a comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue, and nothing in it is even close to the definition, which is why the quoted span is left empty.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely states that appropriated funds are available according to existing appropriations laws. It does not establish any new process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. There is no mention of public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: Appropriations made by section 101 shall be available to the extent and in the manner which would be provided by the pertinent appropriations Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "pertinent appropriations Act" implies a process involving Congress or the public, but the text itself only describes the availability of funds based on existing law. It does not describe any specific participatory mechanism (like a hearing, comment period, or advisory board) within this section. The section is purely administrative regarding fund availability.
